results.problem: Traceback/witness reconstruction for width-bounded DP DAGs
results.quote: Under Assumptions 1 and 2, the Universal Hirschberg algorithm computes a canonical optimal witness path to t using space $\mathsf{SPACE}_\mathrm{traceback}=O(\omega\mathrm{log}T+\mathrm{polylog}T)$, measured in tape cells over a fixed finite alphabet.

results.problem: Asymmetric sequence alignment on an m x n grid (m <= n)
results.quote: an optimal alignment between A and B, runs in time polynomial in mn, and uses space $\mathsf{SPACE}=O\big(mlog(mn)+polylog(mn)\big)$, measured in tape cells over a fixed finite alphabet.

results.problem: One-dimensional recurrence traceback on a chain of length T
results.quote: the witness sequence can be reconstructed deterministically in space $\mathsf{SPACE}=O\big(polylogT\big)\\text{\textit{cells}}$.

results.problem: Banded global alignment on an N x N grid with bandwidth B
results.quote: an optimal alignment confined to the band can be reconstructed deterministically in space $\mathsf{SPACE}=O\big(Blog(BN)+polylog(BN)\big)$.

results.problem: Traceback on DP DAGs of bounded pathwidth
results.quote: an optimal witness path to any sink can be reconstructed in space $\mathsf{SPACE}=O\big(pw(G)log|V|+polylog|V|\big)$.
Then A must use $\Omega(\omega)$ bits of work-tape space in the worst case.
